original_question: Classify all finite modular lattices in which every interval is self-dual, and likewise classify all finitary modular lattices with finite covers in which every interval is self-dual.
target_in_paper: Problem 20 in Section 2 ("Problems of 2025") of arXiv:2509.25446: "[Stan2012, Ch. 3 Exer. 155(c)] Find all finite modular lattices for which every interval is self-dual. Do the same for finitary modular lattices with finite covers."
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem listed in the paper: it asks for a classification of finite modular lattices with the property that every interval is self-dual, and it also includes the notebook's added finitary modular / finite-covers variant. It stays narrow, order-theoretic, and does not drift into broader neighboring lattice questions.
missing_details: State explicitly that the classification is up to lattice isomorphism.
Define "self-dual interval" precisely: for every x <= y in L, the closed interval [x,y] should be order-isomorphic (equivalently, lattice-isomorphic) to its dual interval [x,y]^*.
Spell out what "interval" means here: every closed interval [x,y] of the lattice, not just proper or nontrivial intervals.

Define the finitary condition explicitly. The notebook does not define "finitary modular lattice" inline, so a stand-alone version should state the intended convention; the natural Worley/EC1-style convention is that every principal ideal is finite.
Define "finite covers" explicitly: each element has only finitely many elements covering it and finitely many elements that it covers.

Make clear that there is no ambient ring, field, grading parameter, homogeneity assumption, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or asymptotic quantifier involved; this is a purely lattice-theoretic classification problem.
refined_question: Classify, up to lattice isomorphism, all finite modular lattices L such that every closed interval [x,y] of L is self-dual, i.e. [x,y] is order-isomorphic to its dual interval [x,y]^*. Likewise, classify, up to lattice isomorphism, all finitary modular lattices L with finite covers—where finitary means that every principal ideal of L is finite, and finite covers means that each element has only finitely many upper covers and finitely many lower covers—such that every closed interval [x,y] of L is self-dual.
justification: This arXiv paper is a notebook of open problems rather than a theorem/proposition paper, so the relevant target is not a conjecture numbered 1.1 but Problem 20 in Section 2. Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact wording. The nearest official formulation is Problem 20 itself, which reproduces Stanley's finite modular-lattice exercise and then adds the finitary modular / finite-covers analogue. The nearby mathematical context comes from Stanley's Exercise 3.155(a)-(c): parts (a) and (b) show that the intended local hypothesis really is "every interval is self-dual," and part (c) is exactly the modular-lattice classification problem. For stand-alone sharpness, the only substantive additions needed are the meanings of self-duality, finitary, and finite covers, plus the implicit "up to isomorphism."
